answer: Proposed validators pay a key only while it holds a 1-TiB graph-encoded shard of the ocean archive, salted to that key. A mesa index commits the shard root; random relic blocks and their linked predecessors must arrive from every key in the same three-second audit window. A farm can rent disks and share its model, but each added key needs another resident TiB plus simultaneous read capacity: one stored copy cannot answer distinct encodings on demand. Missing or late proofs forfeit that key's epoch pay. Independent auditors sign timings; validators enforce this, not MinePoA today.
